objective: Replace the current intern-only job discovery bottleneck with a high-recall, multi-stage discovery pipeline that keeps deterministic safety/dedupe controls but restores the semantic breadth Mukund previously got from Codex. The target architecture is: broad collection -> light deterministic prefilter -> DeepSeek bulk semantic triage -> Codex review only for ambiguous/high-value candidates -> deterministic eligibility/visa/clearance gates -> shared dedupe -> tracker/Chief brief handoff. Preserve current Career Ops/Company Watch infrastructure; do not rebuild it.
prerequisites: Reuse career-ops/regional_job_search.py, tracker_writer.py, Company Watch, E2/E3 routing/qualification interfaces and current regional schedules.
Do not require the seven missing provider keys for phase-1 engineering; DeepSeek and Codex are already available/evidenced.
allowed_scope: Inspect the real Career Ops install portals.yml/title_filter and current regional_policy.json first. Treat the existing positive=[Intern, Internship] rule as a precision filter that currently causes false zero-result outcomes when used as a required discovery gate.

Implement a TWO-TIER title policy. Tier A high-recall discovery must accept plausible early-career cybersecurity/IT-security role families without requiring the literal words Intern/Internship. Tier B hard negatives must continue rejecting clearly senior/leadership titles. Keep the original strict intern-only policy available as an optional narrow mode, not the default discovery mode.

Add explicit role-family coverage for at least: graduate/new-grad, junior/associate, analyst/analyst I/L1, SOC/security operations, information security/cybersecurity, GRC/governance/risk/compliance, IAM/identity, vulnerability, technology risk, security consulting graduate/analyst, and closely related entry-level security titles. Do not accept a role solely because it contains the generic word 'security' if another title signal makes it clearly non-cyber or senior.

Do not make title matching the final eligibility decision. The high-recall deterministic filter should only remove obvious bad matches (senior/principal/director/head/manager where genuinely managerial, explicit multi-year requirements when supplied, hard clearance/citizenship conflicts, wrong geography).

Create a structured semantic-classification contract with explicit labels such as strong_entry_level_match, plausible_entry_level, ambiguous_review, too_senior, wrong_discipline, hard_eligibility_block. Every classification must carry source fields, reasons, confidence/uncertainty, and model/provider provenance. Never invent JD facts that are absent from the source record.

Use DeepSeek as the bulk semantic classifier for the candidate pool because it is the high-volume workhorse. Route only ambiguous/high-value candidates to Codex for second-pass review. Codex must NOT be called for every scanned posting. Define deterministic escalation conditions and a bounded per-run Codex budget.
Where a full JD/description is unavailable, classify only from the fields actually present and mark missing-JD uncertainty explicitly. Do not claim semantic JD analysis without source text.

Keep hard deterministic eligibility after semantic classification: region/location, work-authorisation state, clearance/citizenship, explicit mandatory experience requirements, and application URL validity remain authoritative and cannot be overridden by AI.
Preserve shared dedupe against canonical workbooks, cross-month ledgers, Company Watch and regional state before any tracker handoff.

Expose run metrics that make zero explainable: discovered_raw, after_hard_negative_prefilter, semantically_reviewed, deepseek_accept, codex_escalated, codex_accept, deterministic_eligibility_pass, duplicates_removed, tracker_candidates, plus rejection counts by reason. A zero must say WHERE the funnel went to zero.
Integrate Company Watch findings into the same semantic/eligibility/dedupe funnel so 19 findings cannot silently become '0 jobs' without an attributable reason.

Add a safe 'compare modes' acceptance command that can run the old strict intern-only filter and the new high-recall pipeline on the same captured candidate set and report recall deltas without writing canonical trackers.

Add regression fixtures covering titles that the old policy wrongly rejected: Graduate Cyber Security Analyst, Junior Security Analyst, SOC Analyst L1, Information Security Analyst, Junior GRC Analyst, Cyber Risk Analyst, IAM Analyst, Technology Risk Graduate; and negative fixtures such as Senior Security Manager, Principal Security Architect, Physical Security Guard, Security Sales Director.

Run isolated tests first, then a bounded live/dry-run evidence pass. Do NOT write canonical trackers during engineering acceptance. If live sources return no candidates, the evidence must still report source/provider coverage and funnel counts rather than asserting no vacancies exist.
Update Career Daily Brief so it can show funnel counts and top semantic candidates, while preserving that any ranking is a policy output rather than a factual claim about the job.
Update state/current_company_state.md, state/full_build_tracker.md and README with the new discovery architecture and exact truth boundaries.

Checkpoint commits in small units. Preserve current canonical workbooks byte-identical through acceptance. External job applications, LinkedIn actions, employer/recruiter contact and account mutations remain forbidden.
stop_conditions: No fabricated jobs, JDs, eligibility, experience, sponsorship or employer facts.
No autonomous application submission or outreach.
No weakening of deterministic work-authorisation, clearance, dedupe or owner-approval gates.
No browser/GUI automation on the owner's machine.
Do not spend Codex calls across the whole raw scan; keep Codex escalation bounded and evidence the count.
Do not edit the owner's external Career Ops install destructively; prefer control-plane overlays/config or a reversible migration with tests.
If the current scanner/provider cannot expose enough source text for semantic classification, record that limitation and build the contract/fallback path instead of guessing.
notes: Owner-directed change after reviewing why previous job agents returned zero while standalone Codex found roles. Current verified evidence: UK scheduled scan can process ~2861 jobs/run, while Company Watch recently found 19 new postings but 0 tracker-eligible under the current intern-only UK title filter. The objective is not to replace Career Ops with Codex; it is to combine Career Ops collection/state/dedupe with DeepSeek bulk semantic triage and bounded Codex second-pass reasoning.
